title: LOPD latent-token and retrieval-count plateaus reduce to capacity saturation and marginal-information redundancy
dead_end_scope: The standalone claim that LOPD's reward jump around 32 latent tokens and its lack of monotonic benefit beyond three retrieved experiences identify a new agent self-evolution threshold or retrieval-dose mechanism merely from the reported sensitivity curves.

fresh_phenomenon_closure.closure_scope: the reported latent-token capacity plateau and retrieval-count plateau only

counter_explanation.statement: LOPD's own construction makes both sensitivity curves direct instances of mature capacity and marginal-information effects. The latent composer compresses variable-length task-experience representations into a fixed number of learned latent tokens, so increasing that token count increases representation capacity and a rise followed by saturation is predicted by information-bottleneck/rate-distortion behavior. Separately, retrieval is exact cosine-similarity top-n over a frozen successful-trajectory bank. Increasing n_ret therefore nests lower-ranked experiences into the retrieved set; each additional item is separately encoded/compressed and then contributes additional latent context. A gain from the first few nearest experiences followed by a plateau or fluctuation is predicted by diminishing marginal relevance, correlated/redundant evidence, and context-capacity tradeoffs. The reported curves do not hold total latent budget fixed while independently varying number of experiences versus tokens per experience, so they cannot identify a new decomposition-specific mechanism.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: Under the same frozen bank, similarity ranking, composer family, task distribution, and training objective, performance should improve while additional representation capacity or additional high-ranked experience contributes useful information, then saturate or fluctuate as marginal information falls or redundant context accumulates. The location of the empirical optimum can move with task/model/bank statistics without constituting a new causal primitive.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: Latent-context utility is governed first by information capacity and marginal nonredundant evidence; a plateau in token count or nested top-k retrieval is not a new self-evolution mechanism unless a matched information-budget decomposition leaves a residual.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Reopen only with a preregistered same-information experiment that fixes total latent-token/context budget and the frozen experience bank while independently varying experience count and tokens per experience (or an equivalent decomposition), matches training/update compute, and shows a held-out difference that rate-distortion, marginal-information, redundancy/correlation, retrieval-rank, and context-budget baselines cannot express. Do not reopen from another unbudgeted K or top-n sensitivity curve.
counter_explanation.scope: LOPD arXiv:2608.13040, especially the learnable latent context construction, Appendix retrieval definition, and EnvScaler sensitivity analysis.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: n_ret changes only the number of independent trials while information is fixed: false; the released method retrieves a nested top-n set and adds lower-ranked experience content.
latent-token K is unrelated to representation capacity: false; K is the number of learned latent tokens produced by the compressor and used as privileged context.
The published curves isolate experience count from total latent-context budget: false; increasing retrieved items while per-item compression is fixed also changes total composed latent context.
The closure says LOPD's learned context is ineffective: false; it closes only a standalone novelty claim based on the two sensitivity plateaus.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only if a source-faithful or independently reviewed experiment fixes total latent information/context budget and frozen retrieval support, independently changes the experience-count versus per-experience-capacity decomposition, matches compute and update information, and yields a repeatable held-out residual beyond rate-distortion, marginal-information, redundancy/correlation, retrieval-rank, and context-budget baselines.

scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: LOPD reports useful sensitivity curves, but the current token-count and retrieval-count plateaus are already predicted by mature representation-capacity and diminishing-marginal-information principles. A new mechanism would require a matched fixed-budget decomposition residual.
